Hi Jordan — thanks again for the productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum:

1) Requirements you flagged:
- PII must not persist beyond session processing (CardioInsights calls this a 0-retention requirement for user-identifying fields).
- Short-term KV logs for routing/diagnostics OK if they are truncated to a custom window (you suggested 4 hours), with strong encryption and limited access.
- EU residency for any stored telemetry or artifacts tied to EU users; global processing acceptable for inference if no PII is stored.
- Need SOC 2 Type II evidence and an initial DPA draft for legal.

2) Proposed path from Redwood: 
- We can evaluate an ephemeral ingestion flow for PII (ephemeral mode / zero-persistence for designated fields) plus a 4-hour configurable KV window for non-PII telemetry.
- We’ll validate whether the KV window triggers any downstream telemetry retention - typically kept encrypted and accessible only to ops with KMS controls.
- I’ve looped in Rishi (engineering) to confirm feasibility and Neha (privacy) to prepare supporting evidence.

3) Next steps / asks from you:
- Confirm whether 4 hours is your preferred KV window or if you need a shorter option (1 hour) for pilot.
- Share the Legal/Procurement contact for DPA routing (I see legal@cardioinsights.com in your footer).
- Would you like us to run a short demo of the ephemeral flow + KV truncation on Friday? I have a 30-minute slot at 10:00am PT and can add our security engineer.

Attach: Mutual-action-plan-draft.docx (stub attached) — please review the proposed milestones.

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa — quick answers and suggested customer-facing language:

1) SOC 2 / DPA: we can provide a SOC 2 Type II excerpt (security + processing controls) and our standard DPA. Attaching a stubbed filename here: SOC2-Redwood-excerpt-2026.pdf. Legal can accept our DPA and we usually negotiate a limited number of redlines; procurement pricing for custom retention is a commercial discussion.

2) Ephemeral / 0-retention on PII: We do support an ephemeral ingestion flow that can be configured at the field level in our pipeline (mark fields as non-persistent). For CardioInsights, we can implement a policy that strips or encrypts PII before it reaches long-term storage and prevents it from being written to logs. Caveats:
- Some debug traces may still contain hashed indicators; we can suppress hashes for sensitive fields on request.
- Audit logs for operational reasons (access events) will still be retained per compliance but can be redacted for identifying content.

Suggested language for Jordan: "Redwood will enable ephemeral ingestion for specified PII fields to prevent persistence and will configure a 2-hour KV telemetry window for non-identifying routing metadata. SOC2 evidence and a standard DPA will be provided for review."

3) KV truncation (Rishi to confirm timeline): initial thought — configurable TTL is an engineering toggle on the KV layer. For a 2-hour pilot we can provision a config flag and test in staging within ~1 week; for production rollout we'd want a short validation window (2–3 weeks) to confirm no impact to latency SLA. If the customer later requests a different window per region, that adds complexity (routing tables + replication considerations).

I’ll attach the SOC2 stub as requested.
